land.text: the Brittonic kingdom of Dumnonia, of which Cornwall had 'formed part' since the early 6th century

predecessors.note: Cornwall page: 'The Battle of Deorham in 577 saw the separation of Dumnonia (and therefore Cornwall) from Wales'. The Dumnonia dossier ends at 710 with a dissolve into this state; Cliopatria's Dumnonia row ends 709.

land.text: Cornwall west of the Tamar: 14 cells that Cliopatria's England shape gains in 947

successors.note: The Cornwall page gives no date for the end of Cornish rule: it says the boundary 'was set by King Æthelstan in 936' at the Tamar, that King Edgar (959-975) 'was able to issue charters the width of Cornwall', and that Cornwall 'was administered as part of England' by the Norman Conquest. 946 is Cliopatria's last year.

keyframe_review.note: 4,538 km2 (it resolves to 14 grid cells, 3,541 km2: the modern county less one north-eastern cell near Bude at 50.9 N). The page's infobox gives 3,562 km2 for the ceremonial county (3,545 km2 for the unitary area); the Cliopatria area is 1.27 times the infobox, inside a factor of two, and the resolved cells match it. The page gives no area for the kingdom. Question left open: the page's William of Malmesbury story (Æthelstan 'fixed the boundary between English and Cornish people at the east bank of the River Tamar') implies Cornish-held land east of the Tamar before 936, which the shape does not show; the Dumnonia page keeps Britons in Devon to the 10th century. The shape stands.

4,538 km2, unchanged. Æthelstan page: after Hereford 'expel the Cornish from Exeter, fortify its walls, and fix the Cornish boundary at the River Tamar' (William of Malmesbury); Thomas Charles-Edwards calls it 'an improbable story'. The Cornwall page: 'the boundary was set by King Æthelstan in 936'. The shape already stops at the Tamar, so nothing changes; Cornwall's last year in Cliopatria is 946, which no page dates.

region.text: Cornwall, the Cornish rump of Dumnonia west of the Tamar

ledger.note: 710: the Britons of Dumnonia are left holding Cornwall. The page's one 710 sentence is garbled ('King Ine of Wessex and his kinsman Nonna in reference to an earlier Battle of Llongborth in 710'); the Dumnonia page the sibling dossier read says 'In 710 Geraint was defeated in battle by King Ine of Wessex'. 710 is Cliopatria's first Cornwall shape; the Cornwall page does not say Cornwall became a separate kingdom then.

946: Cornwall passes to England on the map. Page silent on the year: the Æthelstan page has the Cornish boundary fixed at the Tamar (a story Charles-Edwards doubts) and the Cornwall page has Æthelstan setting it in 936 and Edgar (959-975) issuing charters 'the width of Cornwall'. The year is Cliopatria's (its Cornwall row ends 946, England's shape gains the Cornish cells in 947).

wars.name: Battle of Hehil
wars.outcome: 'The Annales Cambriae report that in AD 722 the Britons of Cornwall won a battle at Hehil.' No border change.
wars.note: The page does not name the opponent; the Annales Cambriae are read as Britons against the West Saxons.

wars.name: Egbert's campaigns in Cornwall
wars.outcome: 815: 'king Ecgbryht raided in Cornwall from east to west' (read as the end of Cornish independence); 825: a battle between the Cornish and the men of Devon at Gafulforda; 838: 'the Cornish and their Danish allies were defeated by Egbert' at Hingston Down. The Wessex dossier carries the vassal tie from 825.
wars.note: No territorial change is drawn: Cliopatria's Cornwall shape is constant 710-946.

wars.name: Æthelstan and the Tamar boundary
wars.outcome: William of Malmesbury: Æthelstan expelled the Cornish from Exeter and fixed the boundary at the Tamar; the Cornwall page dates the boundary to 936 and doubts the burning of Exeter.

certainty.note: The only candidate for a sharp line is the Tamar boundary of 936 (Cornwall page), a story the Æthelstan page records sceptical historians doubting; no earlier frontier is dated.

sources.title: Cornwall

sources.title: Æthelstan

notes: Two pages budgeted and used. Capitals are an empty list: no opened page names a seat of the Cornish kings (the last recorded king is Dumgarth, drowned 875, per the Cornwall page). Rulers omitted: no list page was opened. The ledger is short because no opened page dates a Cornish border move: the Wessex dossier carries the vassal tie from 825 (vassal_start; it needs its own vassal_end, which is not Cornwall's to record) and the England dossier the 947 gain; the Cornwall page's own end is only 'administered as part of England' by 1066. Disagreements: Cornwall page puts Dumgarth's death at 875 ('drowned') and the Æthelstan boundary at 936; the Æthelstan page treats the Tamar story as doubtful; Cliopatria ends Cornwall 946. Region names: all in the gazetteer. Quotation marks enclose strings the page-fetch tool returned as quotations; other wording paraphrases its summary of the page, which was read by WebFetch only (no raw page text).
